quest.title: Popular Entertainment
quest.description: Petit Lumiere seems to have read something about Flash Cuts in The Steambird...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: I have some bad news. According to a street survey I had The Steambird run, people don't seem all that enthused about the art form that is Flash Cuts.

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: That's really odd. I mean, everyone I talk to says they enjoyed the final cut they saw, but the moment I ask if they're interested in the production, they suddenly sound a lot less enthusiastic...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, really? But Flash Cuts are so much fun to make!

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: The data shows that for most people, the second biggest obstacle is equipment. After all, not everyone is proficient in film kamera operations and post-production...

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: And the greatest obstacle of them all is that people just don't see what they can get out of it, especially since it's hard to share whatever output they create with the people around them.

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: Sharing, huh... I know! We could put together a Flash Cuts Festival! That'd be a way for everyone to feel like their work is being seen and appreciated.

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: Yes, let's do that! We're going big or going home!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, hey! You can't "go big" for everything!

choices.text: But very few people in an audience actually attend a festival.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Like Ms. Paimon, I also think that an event like this has a barrier to entry that isn't exactly low — not just for us, but for the audience we're trying to reach too.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Moreover, the general atmosphere and life cycle of an event like this are also a little removed from the lives of the masses. What we need are examples that cater more to the average man or woman in the street.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: And if we're talking about the average man or woman in the street... the most popular form of entertainment in Fontaine has to be The Steambird. It's just that this particular medium seems...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe we can edit everyone's works into a compilation reel! Then you can watch it with a whole bunch of friends!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: That's right. And maybe we can place it at the start of other short films, just like they do with ads at the cinema. In short, I think there are plenty of platforms and media channels we can choose from!

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Looks like there's still plenty of room for Flash Cuts as an art form to grow. This is truly gratifying to know...

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, thank you! Thank you for helping me identify my next goal!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, all we did was to blurt out a couple of ideas, really.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Please don't worry. We'll definitely invite you onboard if this works out! I also promise to put you two at the very top of our guest list.

choices.text: Just make sure we're well remunerated for this.
Besides, a festival is something that happens only once in a blue moon.
